_comment: A small, deliberately short list of well-sourced seasonal facts. Quality over quantity -- each entry below was researched against a named, checkable source, not generated. That leaves real gaps in the calendar (nothing for spring wildflowers, spring runoff as its own topic, winter beyond the eagle entry, etc.) -- better to have a short list you trust than a long one padded with guesses. Add more entries the same way: find a real source, quote/cite it, don't invent a 'fun fact' from nothing.

entries.headline: The hummingbirds are moving through.
entries.fact: Rufous hummingbirds pass through the San Juans in July and August on their southbound migration -- one of the longest migrations relative to body size of any bird. Broad-tailed hummingbirds, Colorado's common high-country breeder, are still around too.
entries.source_name: Cornell Lab of Ornithology / Rove.me regional migration guide
entries.confidence_note: Timing corroborated across sources; the 'longest migration relative to body size' claim is well-established in ornithology literature generally, not tied to one single citation.

entries.headline: It's elk rut season.
entries.fact: Bull elk spar for dominance over harems of cows this time of year, with mating wrapped up by mid-October. Bugling -- a long, eerie whistle-scream echoing off the ridgelines at dawn or dusk -- is the sound most associated with the rut in Colorado's high country.
entries.confidence_note: The cited CPW page confirms sparring for dominance and mating ending by mid-October, but doesn't itself describe bugling or a specific September start -- the bugling description is common, widely-documented elk behavior in Colorado rather than a direct quote from this source.

entries.headline: Fall color is turning.
entries.fact: Aspens -- about 20% of Colorado's forest cover -- usually peak in the San Juans from late September into early October, running roughly from Silverton (mid-September) down through Pagosa Springs and Durango (early-to-mid October).
entries.source_name: San Juan National Forest fall colors report, USDA Forest Service
entries.confidence_note: USFS report doesn't call out Vallecito specifically; it sits geographically between the Silverton and Durango/Pagosa timing windows cited.

entries.headline: Eagle season at the lake.
entries.fact: Bald eagles are in Colorado year-round, but winter is prime viewing near reservoirs and open tailwaters below dams, where they gather -- sometimes communally roosting in large trees for warmth -- as other water freezes over.
